stages.name: Independent peoples
stages.desc: Berber and desert peoples outside Roman or royal rule

stages.name: Mauretanian kingdom
stages.desc: The Moorish kings: Bocchus and Bogud, then Juba II, Cleopatra Selene and Ptolemy

stages.name: Ptolemaic Egypt
stages.desc: Cleopatra's kingdom and the lands Antony granted her children

stages.name: Roman province
stages.desc: Ruled by a Roman governor or prefect

states.name: Morocco
timeline: King Bogud rules western Mauretania from Tingis (Tangier) as Caesar's ally
Bogud sides with Antony; Bocchus II seizes his kingdom with Octavian's blessing
Bocchus II dies and leaves Mauretania to Rome; Octavian settles veterans in new colonies
Augustus gives Mauretania to Juba II, who marries Cleopatra Selene
Purple-dye works on the Mogador islands, the Purpurariae of Pliny
Caligula kills King Ptolemy; Rome annexes the kingdom and Aedemon rises in revolt

states.name: W. Sahara
timeline: The Autololes and other Berber peoples of the Atlantic Sahara, beyond any king's reach
Juba's ships sail down this coast toward the Fortunate Isles, the Canaries

states.name: Libya
timeline: Cyrenaica is a Roman province; the cities of Tripolitania pass to Roman Africa
In the Donations of Alexandria, Antony names six-year-old Selene queen of Cyrenaica
After Actium, Antony's legions in Cyrenaica go over to Octavian
Balbus campaigns against the Garamantes of the Fezzan

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Caesar wins at Thapsus; Africa Vetus, Carthage's old land, is joined by Africa Nova
Augustus refounds Carthage as a Roman colony
Tacfarinas of the Musulamii begins a seven-year revolt

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Bocchus II rules eastern Mauretania from Iol; Rome takes Juba I's lands around Cirta
Bocchus II dies; Mauretania passes to Rome, which plants colonies along the coast
Juba and Selene make Iol, renamed Caesarea, their royal capital
Cleopatra Selene dies and is laid in the royal mausoleum near Tipasa
The Gaetulian War: Roman troops crush a tribal revolt against Juba
Tacfarinas is killed at Auzia; Rome honours King Ptolemy as an ally
Ptolemy is murdered; Rome annexes Mauretania (made two provinces in AD 42–44)

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Cleopatra VII rules Egypt from Alexandria, the last of the Ptolemies
Cleopatra gives birth to twins, Alexander Helios and Cleopatra Selene
Octavian takes Alexandria; Egypt becomes Rome's, ruled by a prefect
Kush raids Aswan; the prefect Petronius strikes back up the Nile

events.title: Battle of Thapsus
events.text: Caesar destroys the republican army and its ally, King Juba I of Numidia, on 6 April 46 BC.

events.title: Juba I dies
events.text: Defeated and shut out of his own cities, Juba I dies in a suicide pact near Zama.

events.title: Caesar's triumph
events.text: Juba I's infant son is carried through Rome in Caesar's African triumph.

events.title: Africa Nova
events.text: Eastern Numidia becomes a new Roman province; its first governor is the historian Sallust.

events.title: Caesar assassinated
events.text: Caesar is killed in Rome on the Ides of March; Cleopatra returns to Egypt.

events.title: Meeting at Tarsus
events.text: Cleopatra sails to meet Mark Antony at Tarsus and wins him as ally and lover.

events.title: Twins are born
events.text: In Alexandria, Cleopatra bears Antony's twins, Alexander Helios and Cleopatra Selene.

events.title: Bogud expelled
events.text: Bogud of western Mauretania backs Antony; Bocchus II takes his kingdom.

events.title: Sun and Moon
events.text: At Antioch, Antony acknowledges the twins, named Helios and Selene: Sun and Moon.

events.title: Donations of Alexandria
events.text: Antony gives kingdoms to Cleopatra's children; Selene is named queen of Cyrenaica.

events.title: Mauretania to Rome
events.text: Bocchus II dies without an heir and bequeaths his kingdom to Rome.

events.title: Veteran colonies
events.text: Octavian settles veterans in a dozen colonies on the Mauretanian coast, among them Zilil.

events.title: Battle of Actium
events.text: Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeats Antony and Cleopatra on 2 September 31 BC.

events.title: Bogud killed
events.text: Agrippa storms Methone in Greece; the exiled king Bogud dies there.

events.title: Cyrenaica defects
events.text: Antony's governor Pinarius Scarpus takes the legions of Cyrenaica over to Octavian.

events.title: Fall of Alexandria
events.text: Octavian enters Alexandria; Antony and Cleopatra take their own lives and Caesarion is killed.

events.title: Triple triumph
events.text: Selene and her twin walk in Octavian's triumph behind an effigy of their dead mother.

events.title: Carthage refounded
events.text: On the ruins Rome made in 146 BC, Augustus founds a Roman colony at Carthage.

events.title: King Juba II
events.text: Augustus makes Juba king of Mauretania; he marries Cleopatra Selene.

events.title: Iol becomes Caesarea
events.text: The old Phoenician port of Iol is renamed Caesarea and rebuilt as a royal capital.

events.title: War with Kush
events.text: Kushite forces raid Aswan; the prefect Petronius marches up the Nile to Napata.

events.title: Coins of a queen
events.text: Selene strikes coins in Greek as Queen Cleopatra, with the crocodile of the Nile.

events.title: Juba's histories
events.text: Juba writes on Libya, Arabia, Rome and the theatre, drawing on Punic books.

events.title: Garamantes defeated
events.text: Cornelius Balbus wins a triumph for his raid on the Garamantes of the Fezzan.

events.title: Purple of Mogador
events.text: Juba sets up dye works on the Purple Islands off Mogador, as Pliny records.

events.title: Fortunate Isles
events.text: Juba sends an expedition to the Canary Islands, named after their great dogs.

events.title: Prince Ptolemy
events.text: Around this time Selene bears a son, named Ptolemy after her royal ancestors.

events.title: Death of Selene
events.text: The queen dies at about thirty-five; a poet writes that the moon went dark in grief.

events.title: Royal mausoleum
events.text: Selene is laid in the great round tomb of the Mauretanian kings near Tipasa.

events.title: Juba in the East
events.text: Juba joins Gaius Caesar's eastern mission and writes him a study of Arabia.

events.title: Gaetulian War
events.text: Gaetulian tribes revolt against Juba; Cossus Lentulus defeats them for Rome.

events.title: Tacfarinas rises
events.text: Tacfarinas, a deserter from Rome's auxiliaries, leads the Musulamii in revolt.

events.title: Co-king Ptolemy
events.text: Ptolemy begins to rule beside his ageing father.

events.title: Juba dies
events.text: Juba II dies after nearly fifty years on the throne; Ptolemy rules alone.

events.title: Tacfarinas killed
events.text: Tacfarinas dies at Auzia; the Senate sends Ptolemy an ivory sceptre and an embroidered toga.

events.title: Caligula emperor
events.text: Caligula, like Ptolemy a descendant of Mark Antony, becomes emperor.

events.title: Ptolemy murdered
events.text: Summoned by Caligula, probably to Lugdunum, Ptolemy is put to death.

events.title: Aedemon's revolt
events.text: Ptolemy's freedman Aedemon raises Mauretania against Rome; Volubilis fights for Rome.

chartNote: Share of the area of six present-day countries (Morocco, Western Sahara, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt), each coloured by the power that held its settled heartland. A simplification: regions are today's boundaries, the deep Sahara lay outside every state, Roman colonies stood inside the Mauretanian kingdom, and Antony's grant of Cyrenaica to Selene (34–31 BC) may never have taken full effect.
